edits.hypothesis: Structured reasoning procedures (break problem into steps, verify constraints, check alternatives) guide the model toward systematic thinking without task-specific content, improving reasoning accuracy across logic/counting/translation tasks
edits.targets_mode: reasoning errors on boolean_expressions, causal_understanding, linguini, shuffled_objects, object_properties
edits.why_not_lower_lever: A skill file is structural guidance separate from prompts; it's a general procedure repository, not prose rewording. Skill is the right component because it provides reusable procedures the model can reference during reasoning.
edits.trigger_condition: Always included in system prompt; activates whenever model reasons through a problem
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) These tasks fail due to reasoning errors; explicit procedures might improve systematic thinking. (preservative) The skill is general and doesn't override working tasks; passing tasks on web_of_lies, object_properties, shuffled_objects use logical reasoning and would benefit if anything. (transfer) Generalizes to any reasoning task—causal chains, logic puzzles, pattern completion.
edits.regression_risk: If skill text is too verbose, token cost increases and triggers cost rule failure like E1/E2. Mitigation: keep skill text minimal and reference it sparingly in system prompt.
edits.mechanism: Structured reasoning procedures (break problem into steps, verify constraints, check alternatives) guide the model toward systematic thinking without task-specific content, improving reasoning accuracy across logic/counting/translation tasks

edits.hypothesis: Returning ONLY the ANSWER line (instead of 1 line before ANSWER to end) further minimizes output verbosity and potential format confusion. Since grader extracts only ANSWER: line, stripping everything else reduces cognitive overhead and format edge cases.
edits.targets_mode: output format confusion and potential extraction ambiguity
edits.why_not_lower_lever: This is control flow / output plumbing (what gets returned), not wording. It's a structural simplification of what the harness outputs to grader.
edits.trigger_condition: Always applied when simplifying output; whenever ANSWER: line is found, only that line is returned
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) F1 worked well on shuffled_objects (2/2); ultra-minimal output removes any remaining context noise. (preservative) Passing tasks return clean ANSWER: lines and lose nothing when context stripped. (transfer) Generalizes to all task types—minimal output is always safer than cluttered output when grader only reads ANSWER line.
edits.regression_risk: Very low. Simpler code is more robust. Loss of '1 line before' context is safe since grader doesn't use it.
edits.mechanism: Returning ONLY the ANSWER line (instead of 1 line before ANSWER to end) further minimizes output verbosity and potential format confusion. Since grader extracts only ANSWER: line, stripping everything else reduces cognitive overhead and format edge cases.

mechanism: Add skill-based reasoning procedures for exploration + ultra-minimal answer output for robustness
